title: Human ECoG speaking consonant-vowel syllables
description: High-density (256-channel) electrocorticography recorded at UCSF from epilepsy patients while they read aloud consonant-vowel syllables. The dataset includes four subject codes and 31 recording blocks stored as NWB files organized in iEEG-BIDS, with hand-marked annotations of syllable onset, consonant-vowel transition and offset. It supports studies of the functional organization of human ventral sensorimotor cortex during speech articulation.
methods_description: Cortical local field potentials were recorded with subdural high-density ECoG arrays and a multichannel amplifier connected to a Tucker-Davis Technologies digital signal processor, sampled at about 3052 Hz. Participants read aloud consonant-vowel syllables (18-19 consonants followed by /a/, /u/ or /i/). Syllable timing was hand-marked from the speech recordings. The files are byte-identical copies of the source NWB files with BIDS sidecars added.
